evidence: Each re-baseline does carry a reason in its commit (47db044, 272e01b, 249b795), and no grown docstring passes the 120-word cap. But the dismissal rests on 'Nothing grew by appending a restatement', and the tree contradicts that. src/CLI/Config.jl:23 reads 'The ECONOMY MODEL is the cheaper AI model the tool's model catalogue names (`Preflight.economy_model`)' and src/CLI/Preflight.jl:501 reads 'The economy model: the cheaper AI model the tool's model catalogue names, on which every lane and hat...'. Both were added in 47db044, whose message says the model 'is defined in Config's map and on economy_model'. Config.jl :: Config grew 162->227 words and was re-baselined, absorbing the second copy. The scan's own message says 'rewrite, do not append'.
what_would_bite: The Config module docstring and Preflight.economy_model's docstring each define the economy model in full. The Config map already links to economy_model, so a pointer would do. The re-baseline in 47db044 recorded that duplicate as the new ceiling, so the ratchet can no longer flag it. If the economy model changes (for example catalog/models.toml's economy entry or its anchor semantics), one of the two definitions can drift from the other. Demote.jl's docstring is similar: it has been patched in 2026-09-09-check-docs-01, 2026-09-11-check-docs-01 and twice in this round, and grew 192->234 words, although RULE.DOC.SHAPE says a docstring patched three or more rounds 'is rewritten whole rather than appended to again'.
